note: Single registry shared by the Python pipeline and the web app. 'why' texts reviewed by JC (23 Nov 2026); keep them neutral and descriptive, and gloss Scots terms on first use, e.g. 'bings (spoil heaps)'. Screen colours start from the Okabe–Ito colour-blind-safe set; see tests/test_palette.py.

layers.name: Terrain
layers.why: The shape of the land determines where water runs, what can be seen from where, and how much earthmoving a large flat building platform would need.

layers.name: Water
layers.why: Many data centres use water for cooling, and any large site changes how rain drains from the land. Rivers, burns (streams), ponds and reservoirs show where water would come from and go to.

layers.name: Buildings
layers.why: Footprints and heights of existing buildings give a sense of scale against which a proposed facility can be judged. Many heights are estimates.

layers.name: Roads
layers.why: Roads carry construction traffic and connect a site to the places around it.

layers.name: Railways
layers.why: Working and disused railways trace earlier industries, such as coal, oil and steel, and their routes have shaped where later development went.

layers.name: Power
layers.why: Substations, high-voltage lines, battery storage and generators often explain why a site is chosen. Large data centres can draw tens to hundreds of megawatts.

layers.name: Industrial residues
layers.why: Mines, bings (spoil heaps), quarries, landfill and old works are what earlier industries left behind. They are part of the landscape and can affect ground stability and contamination.

layers.name: Schools, care and community
layers.why: Planning assessments treat schools, care homes, hospitals and community buildings as sensitive to noise, light, traffic and air quality. Only the type of building is shown, never names or addresses of homes.

layers.name: Land cover
layers.why: Farmland, woodland, heath and industrial ground show how the land is used now.

layers.name: Planning allocations
layers.why: Local development plans zone land, for example as 'employment land'. Seeing those zones shows how the plan describes the site.
